info.title: Locio API
info.summary: Australian address autocomplete, validation and geocoding.
info.description:
Address and locality search across Australia, and the post offices, parcel lockers and posting boxes to send things from.

Address data comes from G-NAF (CC BY 4.0, Geoscape Australia), localities from GeoNames (CC BY 4.0) and places from OpenStreetMap (ODbL) and operator feeds. Attribution travels with the data: whatever you build shows those credits where the data appears.

Every response is JSON. Errors are RFC 7807 problem documents.

get.description:
G-NAF only. Unlike `/v1/typeahead`, which also returns suburbs and places, every result here is a resolved address, so nothing has to be filtered out.

Matching is a prefix of the street line, so type it as it is written: number first, then the street. A unit in front is understood and resolves to the unit's own record, not the building's: `3/90 Bay Road` returns the pid of unit 3, and `90 Bay Road` returns the pid of the parcel. `unit 3`, `u3`, `apt 3` and `3 90` are read the same way. A trailing postcode narrows.

Each result carries its `id`. Store that, not the text: the text is however your user typed it that day, the id is the address. An Australian result carries the same value under `address_detail_pid`, which is G-NAF's own column name.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description:
Which country's addresses to search, as a two letter ISO 3166-1 code. Defaults to `AU`.

Only a secret key may send it. A public key is scoped to the country the request came from, which Cloudflare resolves from the browser's address, and this parameter is ignored on one: a key that sits in a page cannot choose what it may see.

A country no address data is loaded for answers 200 with an empty `data`, a `country_code` and a `note` saying so. That is not an error: it is the right answer for somebody typing from a country you do not hold.

country_code.description: The country these results were searched in. `AU` today. Distinct from an address's own `country`, which is the country's name.

note.description: Why the answer is empty when empty is correct: no address data is loaded for this country, or the country could not be determined. Absent on an ordinary answer.

get.summary: Resolve a whole address string to one record
get.description:
For an address you are holding rather than one being typed: a delivery address off a checkout form, a row in a spreadsheet.

Give the whole thing, however it is written. Abbreviations, missing commas and a missing state are all fine; where the street ends and the suburb begins is worked out by trying the readings against G-NAF.

This answers validation, geocoding and parsing in one call, because they are one question: `matched` says whether the address is real, and `address` carries the coordinates, the components and the pid. It is one unit, not three.

get.summary: Find addresses close to one that is misspelled
get.description:
For when `/v1/addresses/resolve` found nothing. An address typed by a person is wrong often enough that "no match" is not a useful final answer: `1 gorge rd sydenhum` is one address, and saying which is the point.

The suburb is corrected first, then street lines within it are scored by similarity. Include the suburb if you have it — it is what keeps this fast, and it is what makes the correction good.

**This is the expensive endpoint.** Every other address call is a prefix seek; this is a similarity scan, and it costs three units accordingly. Call it once on an address that failed to resolve, never on a keystroke — use `/v1/addresses` for that.

get.summary: Retrieve one address by its id
get.description:
The pid a search or a resolve returned. This is the endpoint that makes storing a pid worthwhile: the address can be read back a year later without knowing how it was originally typed.

A 404 means G-NAF retired the id between releases, which does happen. Search for the address again to get its current one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id from a result you stored. In Australia that is G-NAF's ADDRESS_DETAIL_PID, which a result also carries under `address_detail_pid`.

get.summary: Suggest addresses, suburbs and places as someone types
get.description:
Two characters minimum: below that the endpoint returns an empty list rather than matching most of the table.

Debounce by at least 150ms in the client. Each request is a unit, and firing on every keystroke spends them for no better answer.

A result whose `kind` is `address` is a resolved G-NAF record, not a string: it carries `gnaf_pid`, coordinates, and `components` holding the address split into G-NAF's own fields. Store the pid against your own record and the two systems agree they mean the same door, whatever either of you does to the formatting afterwards.

Address matching is a prefix of the street line, so type it the way it is written: the number first, then the street. A unit in front is understood and resolves to the unit's own record, not the building's: `3/90 Bay Road` returns the pid of unit 3, and `90 Bay Road` returns the pid of the parcel. `unit 3`, `u3`, `apt 3` and `3 90` are read the same way. A suburb name or a postcode alone matches suburbs, not addresses.
Hints only. The key itself exists in the response that created it and nowhere else.

get.description: What each plan includes: units a month, requests a second, overage rate and export cadence. Public, and the same numbers the meter enforces.

apiKey.description: A key from https://locio.com.au/account/api. Send it as Authorization: Bearer lc_live_… A secret key belongs on your server; a public key may appear in a page and is limited to the origins you name.

session.name: locio_session
session.description: The browser session from signing in. These endpoints manage keys and cannot themselves be called with one.

Unauthorized.description: No key, or not a valid one. Revoked and unknown keys answer the same way.

QuotaExhausted.description: The period's units are spent. X-Quota-Reset says when they return. Distinct from 429 so a client can tell "buy more" from "slow down".

RateLimited.description: Too many requests a second. Back off for Retry-After seconds; refused requests are not charged.

kind.description: What was matched. An address may sit in a suburb with no page of its own, which is why locality_name and state are text beside a possibly empty slug.

gnaf_pid.description: The G-NAF Address Detail PID, on address results only. This is the id to store against your own record: it is stable across G-NAF releases for an address that has not changed, so two systems holding it agree they mean the same door.

components.description: The address split into G-NAF's own fields, on address results only. Absent when the record predates component storage, which is a different statement from present-and-empty: it means this address has not been parsed, not that it has no unit or street type.

hint.description: Enough to tell two keys apart, useless to a thief.

key.description: Shown once. Not stored and not retrievable.

price_cents.description: AUD cents a month, excluding GST.

units.description: Units included each period. A typeahead call is one unit; GeoJSON is one per hundred features.

overage_allowed.description: Free hard stops. Paid plans bill for overrun, capped at twice the plan price.

overage_cents.description: Cents per overage_units beyond the plan.

AddressComponents.description: One address in G-NAF's field names, so it can be checked against the published schema rather than guessed at. Every field is optional: most Australian addresses have no flat and no level, and G-NAF holds properties with no street number. Values are cased for printing, not in G-NAF's upper case.

building_name.description: G-NAF's own name for the building, where it has one. It leads the address: "Piermont Resort, Unit 9, 12990 Tasman Highway".

number_last.description: The far end of a range; 435-437 is number_first 435 and number_last 437.

street_name.description: The name alone, without the type: Sydney, not Sydney Road.

street_suffix.description: A direction, where the street carries one.

locality_name.description: The suburb. Repeated here so an address maps into your own type from one object.

lot_number.description: The lot, for an address identified by one rather than by a street number. On a new subdivision it is the only number the address has, and `formatted` writes it as "Lot 3".

id.description: The id of this address in its country's register, and the one key every address carries. In Australia it is G-NAF's ADDRESS_DETAIL_PID, written under `address_detail_pid` as well. Another register numbers its addresses its own way, and those ids appear under `id` alone. Ids are unique within a country, so store the `country_code` beside it.

address_detail_pid.description: G-NAF's ADDRESS_DETAIL_PID. This is the id to store against your own record: it is stable across G-NAF releases for an address that has not changed, so two systems holding it agree they mean the same door. Not to be confused with gnaf.primary_pid, which identifies the parcel this address sits on rather than this address.

gnaf_pid.description: Former name for address_detail_pid. Same value. Removed in the next release.

formatted.description: The address on one line, as it would be written on an envelope. Composed from the components, so the two can never disagree.

country.description: The country, as a name. Absent when this address sits outside the areas the directory has seeded.

region.description: The state or territory, as a name. Absent when this address sits outside the areas the directory has seeded.

mesh_block.description: The ABS mesh block: the smallest geographic unit the census publishes, and the join key to ABS statistics about the area.

country_code.description: Which register this address came from, as a two letter ISO 3166-1 code. Absent on an Australian record, which is the default. The G-NAF specific fields -- `address_detail_pid`, `gnaf_pid`, `mesh_block` and `gnaf` -- appear only on Australian records.

GNAFRecord.description: The rest of the G-NAF row: the parcel it sits on, whether it is a unit under another address, and how the coordinate was derived. Absent on a record loaded before this was carried.

date_created.description: When G-NAF first published this address.

address_site_name.description: G-NAF's name for the site, where the address is part of a named one: a school, a hospital, a caravan park.

legal_parcel_id.description: The title reference for the parcel, and the join to a state land registry.

alias_principal.description: Whether G-NAF treats this as the principal record for the address or as an alias of one. Only principal records are served.

primary_secondary.description: SECONDARY means the address is a unit under another. 90 Bay Road, Sandringham is one PRIMARY parcel and five SECONDARY units.

primary_pid.description: The gnaf_pid of the parcel this address sits under, on a SECONDARY record. The only thing in the data saying several addresses are one building.

geocode_type.description: How the coordinate was derived. The difference between a pin on the door and a pin in the middle of the property.

tags.name: G-NAF Addresses
tags.description: Australian addresses from G-NAF, the Geocoded National Address File: the national address register, the same source Australia Post and the ABS work from. Resolve one to its G-NAF id, coordinates, ABS mesh block and structured fields. This is the product; everything below it is either a convenience over it or the plumbing around it.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: One box over addresses, suburbs and places at once. Use this when you do not know which of the three somebody is typing; use Addresses when you do.
